# EDGAR Terminal

> Public, source-aware research tools for SEC filings, company fundamentals, market diagnostics, and portfolio analysis.

## Primary research surfaces

- [Market overview](https://secedgarterminal.com/market): SEC fundamental briefing, sector heatmap, company screener, and interactive EDGAR Quant Lab.
- The Market briefing, sector heatmap, Companies and Quant Lab share the prepared expanded SEC issuer universe. Primary sectors are mutually exclusive; optional research themes cover overlapping subsets. Preserve each metric's eligible count, since not every issuer has every measure.
- [EDGAR Quant Lab methodology](https://secedgarterminal.com/market/factors): Definitions, equations, eligibility rules, limitations, and interpretation guidance for regression beta, filing-event response, and the EDGAR Evidence Gap.
- [Research guide](https://secedgarterminal.com/help): Product scope and data-source guidance.
- [About and data sources](https://secedgarterminal.com/about): Provenance, methodology, and project information.

## Machine-readable interfaces

- [Market fundamentals](https://secedgarterminal.com/api/market-research): Compact current TTM and annual financial metrics, source clocks, primary sectors, research themes and dated coverage metadata for the same universe as Quant Lab. Company evidence is available with ?ticker=AAPL. Aggregate requests read prepared caches and never launch a bulk SEC refresh.

- [Quant Lab universe API](https://secedgarterminal.com/api/v1/factor-universe?basis=ttm): Default market-wide snapshot with SEC breadth, paired dispersion, exposure distributions, fixed-sample pairwise correlations and source-linked constituents. Supports only basis=ttm or basis=annual.
- [Universe JSON Schema](https://secedgarterminal.com/schemas/factor-universe-v1.schema.json): Contract for edgar.factor-universe.v1.


- [OpenAPI](https://secedgarterminal.com/openapi.json): Public endpoint description.
- [Market signals JSON Schema](https://secedgarterminal.com/schemas/market-signals-v1.schema.json): Versioned response contract for `GET /api/v1/market-signals`.
- Example: `https://secedgarterminal.com/api/v1/market-signals?ticker=MSFT&window=3y&basis=ttm`

## Interpretation rules

- Preserve dates, units, sample counts, model versions, confidence intervals, provider provenance, SEC accessions, warnings, and null values.
- Do not turn missing values into zero.
- The market model uses raw log returns, not excess returns; its constant is a regression intercept, not Jensen alpha.
- The current SEC filing score is a descriptive peer-normalized snapshot, not a historical factor-return series.
- Filing-event timing is explicit: only timestamped pre-open filings may use that session; intraday, post-close, non-trading-day, and date-only filings use the next benchmark session. Missing expected intervals withhold the affected horizon.
- Benchmark sessions are inferred from observed SPY dates rather than a separately licensed official exchange calendar.
- Peer filing changes use the latest point-in-time company snapshots available at calculation time, not an event-time historical cross-section. Preserve the peer filing-clock fields and non-coeval warning.
- The EDGAR Evidence Gap is a diagnostic comparison, not a valuation, forecast, recommendation, or trade signal.
- Bulk vendor price histories are not distributed through the market-signals API; it returns derived statistics and compact chart points.

## Interpreting the market-wide Quant Lab
- Start with scopes.all.brief and breadth. Values use percentage points; percentages are 0–100. Exposure R², annualized residual volatility and event returns use decimals.
- Growth acceleration is a change in growth rates; it does not mean revenue increased. Cash-flow and book-equity ratios are not standalone health scores.
- Expanded Quant Lab coverage targets the SEC issuers represented in published IVV, IJH and IJR equity holdings. Read universe.coverage for the source dates, target/loaded/missing counts and membership_id. These are fund holdings, not certified current index membership. Expanded groups use the fund-reported sectors; legacy snapshots use curated primary groups. Each CIK counts once.
- Dispersion compares the same paired issuers at their current and comparable prior periods. Observed snapshot history is not a point-in-time backtest.
- The universe filing map uses absolute selected metric change, not peer-normalized z. scopes.all.map describes revenue-growth acceleration; other selected metrics require their own eligibility filter.
- Preserve the co-movement issuer/pair set, coverage and dates. It is actual company-pair correlation, not the median correlation with SPY.
- Characteristic Spearman associations are descriptive, unadjusted and not predictive, causal, significance tests or factor premiums.
- Status partial can still contain useful SEC breadth. Inspect section coverage and retain unavailable values.
- The default universe exposure model uses 252 SPY intervals with at least 240 exact matches. Company drilldown calendar-year windows can differ.

## Interpreting individual company drilldowns
- `reading_guide` includes a version, three summary findings, coverage checks, and per-metric `meaning`, `reading`, and `caution`. Preserve these limitations when summarizing.
- Beta measures historical market sensitivity; R² measures in-sample variation captured, not forecasting accuracy. The 95% beta interval is coefficient uncertainty, not a return prediction interval.
- Above-peer filing change may still be an absolute decline. Read current, prior, and raw change before saying fundamentals improved. The Evidence Gap is a difference of scaled diagnostics, not a statistical z score or expected alpha.
- Input completeness grades measure available evidence, not business quality. Conditional, market and sector models can use different samples.

## Absolute quantitative diagnostics (method factor-universe-1.2.0)
- Quant Lab is the new display name for Factor Lab. Existing /market?tab=factors, /market/factors and API URLs remain valid.
- Keep breadth, magnitude and dispersion separate. Net direction balance = 100 × (higher − lower) / eligible; it is measured in percentage points, not expected return. Zero can mean offsetting increases and decreases.
- Compare growth and cash-margin higher shares only on cash_confirmation's matched operating-issuer sample. Its nine cells include neutral outcomes; each supplies the actual tickers. A lower FCF margin can reflect investment and does not imply declining FCF dollars.
- Default API direction threshold is zero. In the UI, cutoff=0.5 or cutoff=1 changes higher/lower classification only; neutral observations stay in the denominator, and raw magnitudes and paired IQR remain unchanged. These are sensitivity settings, not significance tests.
- The revenue-growth IQR measures dispersion of growth-rate levels; their changes measure acceleration.
- Group variance uses the identical issuer/group sample at both dates with population denominators: total = within + between. Units are squared percentage points; IQRs are not additive. Variance is sensitive to extremes. Shares are null at zero total variance.
- Preserve original SEC, price and calculation dates on an upgraded cached snapshot. New diagnostics do not mean fresh underlying observations.
- JSON downloads include analysis_settings, selected_diagnostics and selected_brief when a user chooses a scope or direction band.

- Membership changes start a new history segment. Do not interpret a larger issuer count as improving fundamentals.
- sec_checked_at is the last issuer filing-history check; facts_retrieved_at is the underlying financial-facts retrieval clock. Reusing unchanged facts does not restamp them.
- SEC eligibility and adjusted-price-model eligibility are separate. Missing financial inputs and unverified price bases remain excluded.
